key_claims: Cerebrospinal fluid, the liquid surrounding and protecting the brain, has reduced flow during sleep in the aging human brain.
Disrupted sleep contributes to the decline in cerebrospinal fluid flow during sleep in aging.
Impaired blood vessel function contributes to the decline in cerebrospinal fluid flow during sleep in aging.
Age-related reductions in cerebrospinal fluid flow can arise through multiple pathways.
limitations: The source text does not detail quantitative effect sizes, demographic characteristics, or specific experimental methodologies.
Surrogate clock scores do not measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
what_not_to_say: Surrogate clock scores measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
Specific medical treatments or lifestyle interventions can reverse the age-related decline in cerebrospinal fluid flow.
